title: Makerspace Network — Space record
description: A makerspace, hackerspace, fab lab, or comparable shared workshop. A profile of Open Know-Where's ManufacturingFacility, extended with the operational fields a directory user actually filters on and with the provenance OKW requires. Crosswalks to OKW, SpaceAPI, fablabs.io and the Entrepreneurship Nexus compact are recorded in docs/INTEROP.md; enum values live in enums.json.

id.description: Stable slug. Never reused, never renamed once published.

name.description: Common name, as the space writes it.

summary.description: One or two sentences, for directory cards.

region_ids.description: Regions this space belongs to, e.g. ['us-ct']. The multi-state tenancy key — the analogue of ecosystem_ids in the Nexus compact.

notes.description: How to actually find the door.

operations.description: The fields a person choosing a space actually filters on, and which the superseded Google Site did not carry.

public_access.description: Can a non-member use the space at all, by any route?

monthly_cost_usd.description: Range across tiers. Always dated — prices rot faster than anything else in this record.

capabilities.description: What can be made here. Granular by design — fablabs.io's six values do not discriminate between spaces.

equipment.description: OKW ManufacturingEquipment. Optional and usually incomplete; capabilities[] is the field the directory filters on.

endpoints.description: URLs the space itself publishes. Where one exists it outranks anything stored here — see the self_managed verification status.

spaceapi.description: SpaceAPI v14/v15 endpoint. Source of live open/closed state.

external_refs.description: This space's identity in other systems. The same reconciliation primitive as external_ref in the Nexus partner API: everyone keeps their own IDs.

standards.description: Participation in the Standards of Excellence framework (tools/standards). Only ever the summary a space chose to share — per-standard scores and evidence never leave the space. See tools/standards/README.md on why. Standards level is also what makes a space a recognised issuer for reciprocity — see docs/RECIPROCITY.md §5.

shared_publicly.description: False by default. A level is published only with the space's explicit consent.

reciprocity.description: Phase 3. Whether this space issues and accepts Open Badges 3.0 credentials for cross-space recognition. See docs/RECIPROCITY.md — the member carries the credential, so neither space needs to integrate with the other.

issues.description: This space signs AchievementCredentials for its own members.

accepts.description: This space will honour credentials issued by recognised issuers in the network.

issuer_id.description: The issuer's identifier in issued credentials — a did:web or an HTTPS profile URL.

public_keys_url.description: Hosted JWKS or DID document. Verifiers fetch this once and cache it; they never contact the issuer per verification.

achievements_aligned.description: Network achievement definition IDs this space issues against, e.g. 'laser-co2-operator/v1'. The space keeps its own local badge names; this records the mapping.

recognised_issuer.description: Derived, not asserted. True when the space's Standards assessment reaches Operational on tool authorisation and hazard assessment. Do not set this by hand — see docs/RECIPROCITY.md §5.

terms.description: Any conditions attached, e.g. 'day access only, no independent after-hours use'.

sources.description: OKW DatabaseSourceMetadata, per record. Where every claim in this file came from.

verification.description: OKW DataVerificator. A directory is only as trustworthy as this field, and stale records are the failure mode that killed every crowdsourced maker map surveyed in docs/INTEROP.md.

verified_by.description: The regional steward or space contact who checked it.

gaps.description: Fields known to be missing or unconfirmed. Being explicit here is why an incomplete record is still publishable.
